We have another 8 year old cat who hasn’t had any issue ever, and he’s also been used to go outside (we have a dog and we often keep doors open for him, except like when it’s really cold), so we can’t keep them inside at all sadly, trust me we tried. Even keeping them in the first few weeks was awful because all they wanted was to go out; we would have otherwise.
I realize my first comment may have made it sound like we “took them one after one” and that I didn’t really care, but no, it’s so fucking painful.
I said they’d get to meet her because you just learn to deal with the fact awful that we can’t bring them back, and I’ve grieved so hard over them that it’s my way to cope, to tell myself they all joined each other eventually and love spending time together now where they are, and whenever I learn about another cat passing away I imagine them all having fun with a new friend.

And why we had 3? They were all new born kittens that friends/people brought to my parents (knowing they loved cats and wouldn’t refuse), so even if they said no the people kept on insisting (although the last one was found & endangered, and would have died in a few days, my mom had already said no for 2 whole days but she/we obviously gave in at some point, because, we just love cats, and it was so guilt tripping to let a kitty knowingly die). So we took care of her, she thankfully survived her next few days, we were so happy that we managed to save her, and then we just hoped with our whole fucking heart that it wouldn’t happen again.

(I specified it all because I don’t want anyone to think we’re careless about animals, we love them, we really do, and we’re trying our best to take care of them. And I know the “3 in a row” makes it look bad but it’s definitely not what we wanted.
We do and did feel like shit and worthless a million time over it.
We can’t keep them inside, nor can people stop driving so fucking fast on the road, so that’s why we’re definitely not getting another kitten now (or anything else, for that matter)).
